question: A previously healthy 8-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of increasing visual loss and deterioration of his hearing and speech over the past 2 months. During this period, he has had difficulty walking, using the stairs, and feeding himself. His teachers have noticed that he has had difficulty concentrating. His grades have worsened and his handwriting has become illegible. His maternal male cousin had similar complaints and died at the age of 6 years. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows hyperpigmented skin and nails and an ataxic gait. His speech is dysarthric. Neurologic examination shows spasticity and decreased muscle strength in all extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are 4+ bilaterally. Plantar reflex shows an extensor response bilaterally. Sensation is decreased in the lower extremities. Fundoscopy shows optic atrophy. There is sensorineural hearing loss bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "8-year-old boy with visual loss and hearing deterioration" -> "progressive neurological symptoms" -> "hyperpigmented skin and nails" -> "ataxic gait and dysarthric speech" -> "spasticity and decreased muscle strength" -> "extensor plantar reflex" -> "optic atrophy on fundoscopy" -> "sensorineural hearing loss" -> "family history of similar symptoms" -> "suggestive of a genetic disorder" -> "possible lysosomal storage disease" -> "Arylsulfatase A deficiency (metachromatic leukodystrophy)" -> 85%

CHAIN: "8-year-old boy with visual and hearing loss" -> "neurological decline over 2 months" -> "hyperpigmentation and ataxia" -> "dysarthria and spasticity" -> "increased deep tendon reflexes" -> "extensor plantar response" -> "decreased sensation in lower extremities" -> "optic atrophy" -> "bilateral sensorineural hearing loss" -> "maternal cousin with similar symptoms" -> "suggests a hereditary condition" -> "consider lysosomal storage disorders" -> "Lysosomal galactocerebrosidase deficiency (Krabbe disease)" -> 80%

CHAIN: "8-year-old boy with progressive symptoms" -> "visual loss and hearing issues" -> "neurological examination shows spasticity" -> "hyperpigmented skin" -> "family history of similar complaints" -> "indicates a possible genetic disorder" -> "consider lysosomal storage diseases" -> "β-Glucocerebrosidase deficiency (Gaucher disease)" -> "less likely due to lack of specific symptoms" -> 70%

CHAIN: "8-year-old boy with visual and auditory decline" -> "neurological symptoms worsening" -> "hyperpigmentation and ataxia" -> "dysarthria and spasticity" -> "extensor plantar reflex" -> "optic atrophy" -> "sensorineural hearing loss" -> "family history of similar symptoms" -> "suggests a genetic disorder" -> "ATP-binding cassette transporter dysfunction" -> "less likely due to symptom profile" -> 65%

CHAIN: "8-year-old boy with visual and hearing loss" -> "progressive neurological symptoms" -> "hyperpigmented skin and ataxia" -> "dysarthria and spasticity" -> "extensor plantar reflex" -> "optic atrophy" -> "sensorineural hearing loss" -> "family history of similar symptoms" -> "suggests a genetic disorder" -> "α-Galactosidase A deficiency (Fabry disease)" -> "less likely due to symptom profile" -> 60%
analysis: The clinical presentation of the 8-year-old boy, including visual loss, hearing and speech deterioration, ataxic gait, dysarthria, spasticity, and decreased muscle strength, along with the family history of similar symptoms and early death, suggests a neurodegenerative disorder. The hyperpigmented skin and nails, along with the neurological findings, are indicative of a lysosomal storage disorder. The symptoms align closely with Metachromatic Leukodystrophy, which is caused by Arylsulfatase A deficiency. This condition leads to the accumulation of sulfatides, affecting the nervous system and causing the observed symptoms. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms is Arylsulfatase A deficiency.
